description: Trims low-level material from the START (everything before the first sample exceeding startgate) and the END (everything after the last sample exceeding endgate) of a file, with splicelen ms fades at the new edges - the gate-driven top-and-tail. Gates are ABSOLUTE linear amplitudes 0-1 compared per sample (source-verified: first/last |sample| > gate x full-scale). Duration is content-dependent (declared 'static' is the conservative placeholder): a syllable train with 50 ms lead silence trimmed 2.0 -> 1.9499 s at gates 0.1; material hot from sample 0 passes through sample-exact. backtrack moves the start cut earlier by up to backtrack ms to catch soft onsets. All four parameters refuse breakpoints. Deterministic; stereo accepted. SEE known_issues FOR THE DOUBLING BUG - the reason to keep startgate low or lead silence real.
musical_use: Batch edge cleanup: strip preroll, count-in bleed, and decaying tails to a known level in one deterministic pass - the standard prep before looping, concatenation (sfedit joins), retiming, or any duration arithmetic that assumes material starts and ends where it sounds. backtrack 10-30 ms preserves the breathy front of soft attacks that a hard threshold would clip. Distinct from the gate program (which zeroes/excises INTERIOR passages too) and housekeep topntail: this one only touches the two ends and leaves everything between the first and last loud sample intact. For fade-shaping rather than trimming, dovetail; for trims at exact times, sfedit cut.

startgate.description: Absolute level (0-1 linear) the signal must exceed for the file to 'start'; earlier material is removed. CDP-enforced 0-1 ('Parameter[1] Value (1.500000) out of range (0.000000 to 1.000000)'). Keep it at or just above the noise floor - see the doubling bug. Breakpoint refused. Scalar only.

endgate.description: Absolute level the signal must exceed for the file to 'end'; later material is removed. CDP-enforced 0-1 (Parameter[2]). Breakpoint refused. Scalar only.

splicelen.description: Fade length applied at the new edges. CDP-enforced 2-200 ms ('Parameter[3] Value (6000.000000) out of range (2.000000 to 200.000000)'). Breakpoint refused. Scalar only.

backtrack.description: Moves the start cut up to this many ms EARLIER than the gate crossing, preserving soft onsets. CDP-enforced 0-1000 ms (Parameter[4]). Breakpoint refused. Scalar only.

examples.expected_use: Preroll and tail below 0.05 removed, 15 ms default splices at the new edges; interior untouched.

examples.description: Trim hard but keep the breath before the note.
examples.expected_use: Cut point backs off 25 ms from the first loud sample - soft consonants/bow noise survive.

known_issues: DOUBLING BUG (first-class, trigger pinned): when the first above-gate sample lies WITHIN ONE SPLICELEN of the file start (0 < startsamp < splicelen samples), the output is the file rendered TWICE - 2.0 s inputs came back 3.99 s of doubled material (verified with a 5 ms lead-silence fixture at gates 0.1; a 50 ms lead trims correctly to 1.9499 s, and startsamp == 0 passes through exactly). Avoid by keeping startgate at/below the level of the very first samples, or ensuring real lead silence longer than splicelen. Source: top_and_tail() in dev/standalone/topantail2.c clamps startsplice to 0 while startsamp stays > 0.

DURATION IS CONTENT-DEPENDENT: output = last-above-endgate minus first-above-startgate (plus splices); the 'static' model is a placeholder that is exact only for material loud at both ends (the findings duration row uses gates 0.01 on the flat fixture: 2.0000 sample-exact).
Gates are absolute linear amplitudes (0-1), not dB and not peak-relative.
Whole-file-quiet refusals exist in source ('At this gate level, entire file will be removed.') - not triggered in probes, quoted from topantail2.c.
All params scalar-only (breakpoints refused, parameters 1-4). Deterministic; stereo accepted.
